title: Huskeys raises $27M Series A led by Blackstone to police AI-agent web traffic
subtitle: The Tel Aviv startup — founded by Unit 8200 alumni — is analyzing a trillion web requests a day. TikTok, LEGOLAND, Hugging Face and Blackstone itself are customers.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Huskeys closed a $27 million Series A led by Blackstone Innovations Investments on September 2, taking total funding to $35 million and its valuation past $100 million. Merlin Ventures, Skinos, Zscaler Ventures, Okta Ventures, Bright Pixel and SV Angel joined the round, along with individual investors from Palo Alto Networks, Cloudflare, Check Point, AWS, Google, Microsoft and Intel — the security-vendor bench of a decade lining up behind one bet.

The bet is that AI agent traffic breaks the assumptions the web was built on. Huskeys, co-founded by Unit 8200 alumni Itai Gafni and Roy Weisfeld, builds tools to distinguish, rate-limit, and block automated requests coming from AI agents at the network edge. The company says it is already analyzing more than a trillion web requests and thousands of network configurations per day across TikTok, LEGOLAND, Ro, Blackstone and Hugging Face.

This is one of several 2026 companies chasing the same category — Cloudflare's Kitesurf browser, Lasso's LEAP CPU guardrails funded last week, JetStream's zero-trust per-action authorization also from last week. The common insight: existing WAF and bot-detection stacks were built for a world where non-human traffic was either scrapers or DDoS, both of which you block. Agent traffic is a third thing — often legitimate, often on behalf of a paying customer, but not a browser session and not something the origin site consented to serve. Someone has to sort it, and that someone is now a fundable line item.

For learners: if you build anything customer-facing on the web, the question 'how do I want AI agents to interact with my site?' is now a design decision, not a hypothetical. Answer it deliberately — a robots.txt line, an agent-tier pricing plan, or nothing at all — before your traffic mix answers it for you. The companies who lose here will be the ones who never noticed the mix change.
